answer: A staking bond makes identity expensive: each agent must lock a deposit in a shared haven before it can transact, and slashing removes the bond when fraud is proven. Reputation then grows only through a slow lagoon of verified, small transactions rather than a sudden plume of cheap accounts, so creating thousands of fake identities costs far more than any single scam can return. Attackers must pay real capital and time for every persona, while honest newcomers build trust gradually at low cost.
